description.p: Termina runs your shell on a real pseudo-terminal and renders it with xterm-compatible emulation. It is the same application on Linux, macOS and Windows.

ul.li: Tabs, split panes and multiple windows
A command palette, and key bindings that can be changed and synced between machines
Scrollback with search, clickable links and file paths, and shell integration
Mouse support for full-screen programs such as vim, less and htop
Built-in and imported colour themes, and a choice of bundled fonts

screenshot.caption: A shell with two tabs, a git-aware prompt and a directory listing

description.p: A full listing in GNOME Software and KDE Discover, with the description, licence and icon. An AppImage and a tarball beside the packages, every download signed, and Ctrl+click opens the URLs in Markdown links.

The macOS app is signed and notarized, every Linux download is signed, and Linux gains an AppImage and a tarball. The packages list properly in GNOME Software, and Ctrl+click opens the URLs in Markdown links.

Padding around the text, a hollow cursor in unfocused panes, Reopen for closed panes and windows, and a title for the first tab with -T. The packages install on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 again, put termina on the path and register it as a terminal emulator.
The settings sync repository can be created on GitHub from Settings, and the shortcut reference names what a middle-click pastes on Linux.
